_comment: Hard-deny policy. Two independent keys: `patterns` matches shell COMMAND strings; `protected_paths` matches the TARGET of a file write (Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit). `protected_paths` is Gate 1a, `patterns` is Gate 1b. Add domain-specific entries below.
_guidance: These are catastrophic-only defaults. Review and extend for your domain.

patterns._note: Roots, not paths under them. Replaces the bare literal 'rm -rf /', which substring mode made wrong BOTH ways: it denied every `rm -rf /<path>` (scratch cleanup) and allowed the roots not spelled with a leading slash (~, $HOME, ., *, ../..). See build design 6.2 item 14. Residual: a scoped absolute path such as /etc is NOT matched, because enumerating system roots re-creates the over-block.

S2.4 shell vector: a file_path check cannot see a shell redirect or in-place edit, so block the obvious command forms that target the harness's own mechanism/policy. Pattern-based and therefore incomplete by nature - see SECURITY.md S2.4 for the residual gap. The Security-kit branch was added 2026-08-17: this family named only governance/ and settings.json, so `echo x > Security-kit/content_trust.py` was ALLOW (measured) even though an Edit to the same file was DENY.

Enumerated rather than a bare `Security-kit/` prefix on purpose: this family includes `rm`, and `Security-kit/` also holds generated files (coverage.json) plus the eval corpus, which a project legitimately deletes and regenerates. Naming the four mechanism entry points blocks the vector without an over-block.

_protected_paths_note: Write targets the agent may never modify - the mechanism and policy that constrain it (S2.4). Paths are project-root-relative and compared by file IDENTITY, so '../', './', absolute forms, symlinks and (on macOS/Windows) case variants all resolve to the same target and cannot smuggle a write past the check. ADDITIVE: permission.py enforces BUILTIN_PROTECTED_PATHS unconditionally, so deleting an entry here (or this whole key) does not unprotect it. Add project-specific files you want frozen.
